original_value: Blast-resistant buildings are mainly used to protect main instruments, controllers, expensive equipment, and people from explosion waves. Oil and gas industry projects almost always include blast-resistant buildings. For instance, based on a hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) analysis of a plant, control rooms and substations are sometimes designed to withstand an external free air explosion that generates blast over pressure. In this regard, a building façade is considered to be the first barrier of resistance against explosion waves, and therefore a building façade has an important role in reducing a building’s vulnerability and human casualties. In case of a lack of enough resistance, explosion waves enter a building and bring about irreparable damage to the building. Consequently, it seems important to study and evaluate various materials used in a façade against the consequences of an explosion. This study tried to make a comparison between different types of building facades against explosion waves. The materials used in a building play a key role in the vulnerability of a building. In this research, a literature review and the fuzzy Delphi method were applied to find the most critical criteria, and then a fuzzy evaluation based on the distance from the average solution (EDAS) was applied in order to assess various materials used in building facades from the perspective of resiliency. A questionnaire was presented to measure effective indices in order to receive experts’ ideas. Finally, by implementing this methodology in a case study, it was concluded that a stone façade performs much better against explosions.

result.paraphrase: Blast-resistant buildings are primarily intended to shield key instruments, control systems, costly equipment, and personnel from blast waves. In oil and gas projects, they are almost always part of the design. For example, after a plant hazard identification (HAZID) and hazard and operability (HAZOP) review, control rooms and substations may be engineered to resist an external free-air explosion that produces blast overpressure. In this context, the building façade is regarded as the first line of defense against explosion waves and therefore plays a major role in reducing both structural vulnerability and loss of life. If the façade lacks sufficient resistance, blast waves can penetrate the building and cause irreparable damage. It is thus important to study and assess different façade materials for their response to explosions. This study compared various building façade types under blast-wave conditions. The materials used in a building are a key factor in its vulnerability. Using a literature review and the fuzzy Delphi method, the research identified the most critical criteria, then applied a fuzzy evaluation based on the distance from the average solution (EDAS) to assess different façade materials in terms of resiliency. A questionnaire was used to measure relevant indicators and gather expert opinions. In the end, the case study showed that a stone façade performs much better against explosions.
